intro.en: Weddings, traditions, beliefs, and the vocabulary of a popular festival.

nota.en: Use de before the character or costume: disfrazarse de pirata.
Use despedida de soltero for a groom and despedida de soltera for a bride; names and customs vary by region.
The stem changes from o to ue in forms such as envuelvo, but not in envolvemos.
In some Spanish-speaking communities, celebrar el santo means celebrating the feast day of one's patron saint or namesake.
Creyente can also be a noun and has the same form for men and women: un creyente, una creyente.
The adjective agrees with the person: ateo, atea, ateos, ateas; it can also be a noun.

soler.en: to usually do; to tend to

nota.en: Soler is followed by an infinitive: se suele bailar (people usually dance).
In Spain, this date is traditionally associated with bad luck; beliefs vary.
When followed by a clause with a different subject, use the subjunctive: es costumbre que los vecinos cenen.

texto.en:
Many towns in Spain celebrate local **fiestas populares**; some honour a patron saint. Events may include **un desfile** or **una procesión**, **música**, **fuegos artificiales** or food in the street. During **Carnaval**, people **se disfrazan de** different characters. Customs vary from place to place.

At a wedding, there may be **la despedida de soltero/a**, **la boda** (civil or religious), **el banquete** and **la luna de miel**. You **felicitas a** the couple: **¡Enhorabuena! ¡Que seáis muy felices!** In Spain, **seáis** addresses **vosotros**; in much of Latin America, people use **ustedes**: **¡Que sean muy felices!**

Presents: **envolver** a gift, **abrirlo** or **hacer un regalo**.

Beliefs: **ser creyente**, **ser ateo**, **ir a misa**, **rezar**. In Spain, some people associate **martes y trece** with bad luck.

Talk about customs with **soler + infinitive**, impersonal **se suele + infinitive**, **es costumbre + infinitive** or **es costumbre que + subjunctive**: **Se suele** cenar tarde; **es costumbre** dar dos besos; **es costumbre que los vecinos cenen juntos**; **es típico** bailar.

frases.es: Cada agosto mi pueblo celebra sus fiestas, que duran una semana.
frases.en: Every August my village celebrates its annual festivities, which last a week.

frases.es: El primer día hay un desfile y los niños se disfrazan.
frases.en: On the first day there is a parade and the children dress up.

frases.es: Por la mañana las personas más creyentes van a misa y luego sale la procesión del santo.
frases.en: In the morning the most devout people go to Mass, then the procession for the patron saint sets off.

frases.es: Es costumbre que los vecinos cenen juntos en la calle.
frases.en: It is the custom for neighbours to have dinner together in the street.

frases.es: La última noche se suele bailar hasta que empiezan los fuegos artificiales.
frases.en: On the last night people usually dance until the fireworks start.

frases.es: Mucha gente que vive fuera vuelve al pueblo solo para las fiestas.
frases.en: Many people who live away come back to the village just for the festival.

pregunta.en: Complete: at Carnival I dress up as a pirate.
Complete: it is the custom for neighbours to dine together.

cenan.en: After es costumbre que, the subjunctive.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Describe a tradition or a superstition from your country and what you think of it.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Explain aloud to a foreigner a festival in your country: its origin, what people do and what they eat.
